about: Golden cases of the forecast model (server/domain/forecast.ts), from the reference implementation it was ported from: synthetic spending, no real data. Samples are [minutes since the epoch, used, reset time in minutes since the epoch, window length in minutes], from 23 days before the last one, unchanged ones in the middle of a run left out (the cells they make are the same). expected.state is the reference's: pace and left are both "lasts" here, the board telling them apart by `comfy`; expected.hours is the reference's history on these samples; memoryOut.X is the share shown when it lasts.

cases.what: Steady spending round the clock: the zero comes before half the time to the reset, red, runs out in hours.
The same steady spending early in the week: the zero comes after half the time to the reset, yellow, the countdown in days.
Weekday work, quiet Saturday and Sunday, Friday 18:00: the shape of the day alone does not know the weekend ahead; the day-of-week factor learns the quiet days from what was spent.
Weekday work, Monday 19:00: after a working day, the weekend is still ahead.
Quiet Tuesday and Wednesday rather than the weekend: on Monday evening the day-of-week factor counts two quiet days ahead.
Weekday work at UTC-7: the working day crosses midnight UTC, and days of the week are UTC days.
Overnight runs: little is spent in the day, but the shape of the day knows the night; the line has shelves.
Speeding up towards the end of the week: in the quiet first days some is left, the share held within its dead band.
The same week after speeding up: runs out.
A burst: the level of the last day is over three times the usual, so the day-of-week factor is off and the zero follows the shape of the day.
A free reset: right after it the pace is known from the history through resets.
The limit is used up and waits for the reset.
The first hours of a new window after waiting at zero: the hours at zero are not in the pace.
An early reset for everyone: a new window, the same pace.
A sleeping laptop: no samples at night, and the forecast stands on the last hour with a sample.
A laptop asleep over the weekend: a gap with no change of what is left is idle time.
The reset fell while the laptop slept: until the first sample of the new window the forecast waits rather than foresee the old one.
Installed on a Wednesday at 11:00 with no history: the first hour says nothing.
The first day after installing: a straight line blended with the window's own mean, weighted n/(n+24).
The second day after installing: the shape of the day is there, the day-of-week factor not yet (under 14 days).
Hysteresis: F rose above -5 but not above +2, so runs out holds.
The dead band of the moment: the zero moved by less than the larger of an hour and a fifth of the time to it, and the moment shown stays.
The dead band of the share: what is left at the reset moved, and the share shown stays.
Just enough: F between -5 and the larger of 5 and 5 a day to the reset.
Running into the five-hour limit at a random phase: the hours of the block stay in the pace as they are.
The cost of the day-of-week factor: after moving from weekday work to overnight runs it still counts the weekend as quiet.
A team in three time zones: nearly round the clock on weekdays, quieter at the weekend.
Weekday work with a realistic spread of days (sigma 0.6).
